examFormat.mix: ~11 concept MCQs (Ch1 analytics + Ch3 charts + Ch8 definitions) · ~8 computation problems (accuracy measures, moving avg, exp smoothing, trend + seasonal regression)
examFormat.notes: Review solutions give exact target numbers — every computation below is verified against them. Calculator work: error tables, k−1 dummy regressions.

verifiedPatterns.pattern: Build the full error table (Forecast, e, |e|, e², |%e|) for a 5-year series under naive / average / moving-average / exp-smoothing, then compute MAE, MSE, MAPE + the year-6 forecast — four consecutive questions use the SAME series (234, 287, 255, 310, 298)
Given quarterly data, code k−1 dummies, run regression, write ŷ, forecast all 4 quarters of next year — with trend (add t) and without
Given a fitted trendline (ŷ = 78.291 + 3.035t), compute MSE over ALL periods (k=0) and forecast t=6
Definition MCQs lifted straight from lecture wording — pattern names, method↔pattern match, analytics types, when to use tables

topics.name: Forecast accuracy measures
topics.why: MFE/MAE/MSE/MAPE tables are 4 of the 8 computation questions. Know the n−k denominators cold.

topics.name: Smoothing methods (naive · average · MA · exp smoothing)
topics.why: One shared 5-year series, four methods. Pattern-match the arithmetic, don't re-derive.

topics.name: Seasonal dummy regression (± trend)
topics.why: Three full problems. Write ŷ from the coefficient table, plug quarters, read forecasts.

topics.name: Time-series patterns → method choice
topics.why: Horizontal→MA/ES · trend→regression on t · seasonal→dummies. Several MCQs test exactly this mapping.

topics.name: Ch1 analytics types + Ch3 chart choice
topics.why: Descriptive/predictive/prescriptive + which chart/table for which data — the first 5 review MCQs.

formulas.name: Forecast error
formulas.vars: y_t actual · ŷ_t forecast for period t
formulas.when: The atom of every accuracy measure — sign matters (+ = under-forecast)
formulas.trap: Order is actual MINUS forecast — flipping the sign flips MFE's bias reading

formulas.name: MFE — bias, not accuracy
formulas.vars: n periods · k = periods with no forecast
formulas.when: Answers 'am I systematically over/under-forecasting?' ONLY
formulas.trap: MFE ≈ 0 does NOT mean accurate — ± errors cancel (gasoline naive: MFE 0.45 but MAE 3.73)
formulas.ex: Coffee shop: errors −10,5,−10,5,10 → MFE = 0 (unbiased), yet MAE = 8

formulas.name: MAE
formulas.when: Average miss in real units; the intuitive one
formulas.trap: Compare methods on the SAME series only — MAE is scale-dependent
formulas.ex: ★ Q12 naive: Σ|e| = 152 over 4 errors → MAE = 38

formulas.name: MSE
formulas.when: Punishes big misses hardest; the tie-breaker the course uses to pick methods and α
formulas.trap: Denominator is n−k, NOT n — a 3-yr MA on 5 years has only 2 errors → divide by 2

formulas.name: MAPE — relative accuracy
formulas.when: Cross-scale comparison (small shop vs Starbucks)
formulas.trap: Divide by actual y_t, NOT forecast ŷ_t
formulas.ex: ★ Q12 naive: MAPE = 13.20% · Coffee 7.5% vs Starbucks 7.0% though MAE 8 vs 76

formulas.name: Naive forecast
formulas.when: Baseline method; k=1 (no forecast for period 1)
formulas.trap: It is NOT 'the accurate simple method' — average beat it on all three measures (gasoline)

formulas.name: Average-of-all forecast
formulas.vars: running mean of ALL history so far
formulas.when: Stable horizontal series; each forecast uses a growing window
formulas.trap: The forecast for year 3 averages years 1–2 only — not all 5 years

formulas.name: Moving average (order k)
formulas.when: Horizontal pattern; small k tracks shifts fast, large k smooths noise
formulas.trap: First forecastable period is t = k+1 — with k=3 on 5 years you get exactly 2 errors

formulas.name: Exponential smoothing
formulas.vars: α = weight on the LATEST actual · start ŷ_2 = y_1
formulas.when: Horizontal pattern; all history weighted, decaying geometrically
formulas.trap: ŷ_2 = y_1 (NOT 0, NOT an average) — the chain starts from the first actual

formulas.name: Exp smoothing — error-correction form
formulas.vars: new forecast = old forecast + α × latest miss
formulas.when: Same formula rearranged — explains WHY α is a reaction speed
formulas.trap: Noisy series → SMALL α (don't chase randomness); stable series → larger α; choose α that minimizes MSE

formulas.name: Linear trend projection
formulas.vars: b_0 intercept · b_1 slope per period · t = time index
formulas.when: TREND pattern (MA/ES are wrong here — they lag a trend)
formulas.trap: Regression forecasts EVERY period → k = 0, MSE divides by all n

formulas.name: Seasonality WITHOUT trend (dummy regression)
formulas.vars: k seasons → k−1 dummies · Q4 = all zeros = baseline b_0
formulas.when: Seasonal pattern, flat plot (no t term)
formulas.trap: Quarter 4's forecast is just b_0 — there is NO Q4 coefficient

formulas.name: Seasonality WITH trend
formulas.formula: ŷ_t = b_0 + b_1Qtr1 + b_2Qtr2 + b_3Qtr3 + b_4·t
formulas.vars: dummies for season + t for growth · t keeps counting across years
formulas.when: Plot shows recurring peaks AND upward drift
formulas.trap: Next-year t values continue the index (year 4 of 3-yr quarterly data = t 13–16, NOT 1–4)

formulas.name: Q19 South Shore — the 5-year version
formulas.when: Same seasonal+trend recipe at scale — negative intercept is FINE
formulas.trap: A negative b_0 does not mean negative forecasts — t·12.138 dominates by year 6

formulas.name: Smartphone seasonal+trend (lecture version)
formulas.vars: slope 0.146 ≈ +146 phones/quarter, same for every quarter
formulas.when: The lecture's worked template for Q17/Q19-style problems
formulas.trap: Dummies shift the INTERCEPT only — all four quarterly lines share slope 0.146

formulas.name: Coffee-shop worked set (all four measures)
formulas.when: The lecture-7 template for 'compute all four measures'
formulas.trap: MFE = 0 here yet MAE = 8 — unbiased is NOT accurate

formulas.name: Umbrella seasonal (lecture worked)
formulas.when: The lecture's Q18-style template
formulas.trap: Q4 forecast = intercept 95 — no Q4 coefficient exists

formulas.name: Bicycle trend (lecture worked)
formulas.when: The lecture's Q16-style template
formulas.trap: Read slope in ORIGINAL units — sales are in 1000s

formulas.name: Average-of-all — the growing window (Q13 chain)
formulas.vars: each forecast averages ALL prior years
formulas.when: Show the chain, then the measures
formulas.trap: F3 uses years 1–2 only — not the full series

formulas.name: ES gasoline chain (lecture α=0.2)
formulas.when: Practice the recursion until it's mechanical
formulas.trap: Round only at the END — chained rounding drifts the answer

formulas.name: Notes workbook — naive on the 10-yr series
formulas.when: Longer drill of the exact Q12 mechanics
formulas.trap: Year 7 alone: e = 206 → e² = 42,436 — one big miss dominates MSE
formulas.ex: Same table shape as the exam: e, |e|, e², |%e| columns

formulas.name: Linear trend — notes Q5 (full output)
formulas.when: Q16-style with real regression output attached
formulas.trap: Forecasting MSE = ΣFE²/n = 35.62/10 = 3.56 — NOT the ANOVA MS (35.62/8 = 4.45)

formulas.name: Seasonal WITHOUT trend — notes Q6
formulas.vars: same 12 quarters as the with-trend fit
formulas.when: Compare against the with-trend version to see why t matters
formulas.trap: R² = 0.138 on trending data — dummies alone can't absorb growth

formulas.name: ES next-step forecast — notes Q4
formulas.when: The 'one more step' ask after the error table
formulas.trap: Use the LAST actual and the LAST forecast — not the last error row

formulas.name: F-statistic (ANOVA)
formulas.when: Overall model significance — pair with Significance F
formulas.trap: A big F still needs its p-value (Significance F) < 0.05 to conclude

formulas.name: Mean Square
formulas.when: Bridge from sums of squares to the F-test
formulas.trap: Residual df = n − p − 1 (10−1−1 = 8), NOT n−1

formulas.name: t-Stat for a coefficient
formulas.when: |t| > ~2 → the predictor matters
formulas.trap: Tests ONE coefficient — the F-test covers the whole model

formulas.name: SSE — residual sum of squares
formulas.when: The quantity regression minimizes; feeds MS_Residual
formulas.trap: SSE is what's LEFT OVER — SS_Regression is what's explained

formulas.name: R² from sums of squares
formulas.when: Connects the ANOVA table to R²
formulas.trap: SS_Total = SS_Reg + SS_Res — don't divide by SSE

formulas.name: Slope 95% CI
formulas.when: Range for the TRUE per-period change
formulas.trap: CI excluding 0 ⇔ significant at 5%

concepts.def: What HAPPENED — dashboards, summary tables, charts of past data.
What WILL happen — regression, time series, data mining, simulation. 'Model from past data to predict future sales' = predictive.
What SHOULD we do — optimization gives the best decision under constraints.
Reader needs exact values · precise (not relative) comparisons · values with different units/magnitudes.
THE table for two variables (any mix of qual/quant); margins define the classes.
categorical compare → bar/column · 2 quantitative → scatter (+trendline) · time series → line · 3 vars in 2-D → bubble · in-cell axis-less trend → sparkline · magnitude by color → heat map.
Observations at successive points/periods of time. Objective: uncover the pattern, extrapolate it forward.
Historical data unavailable OR not applicable. (Quantitative needs: data available, quantifiable, past-is-prologue.)
Horizontal (random around constant mean) · Trend (long-run drift) · Seasonal (recurring by period) · Trend+Seasonal. Plot FIRST, then pick the method.
Small k = tracks level shifts quickly · large k = smooths random noise. Adapts to a new level in k periods.
Much random variability → small α (don't overreact) · stable series → larger α (react fast). Formally: pick α minimizing MSE.
A categorical with k levels needs k−1 dummies — 4 quarters → 3 dummies, omitted level becomes the intercept.
Interval = real numbers, all arithmetic meaningful. Nominal = labels/categories — calculations meaningless (marital status coded 1/2 is still nominal).
Axis-less mini line chart living in a single cell; shows trend only, takes minimal space.
2-D grid where COLOR SHADE carries magnitude.
THREE variables in 2-D — the bubble size is the third variable; preferred over 3-D graphs.
Collection of tables/charts/maps + summary stats that UPDATE as new data arrive — descriptive analytics.
Both PREDICTIVE tools: mining finds patterns in large databases; simulation models uncertainty with probability.
Past data available · quantifiable · past is prologue (pattern continues).
Line approximating the relationship between two quantitative variables on a scatter chart.
R² penalized for extra predictors. Close to R² (0.919 vs 0.928) = stable model; big drop = junk variables.
Average distance between actual and predicted y, in y's units — ±2.11 IP points typical miss.
p-value for the WHOLE model. < 0.05 → model beats random noise (7.5E-06 in notes Q5).
|t| > ~2 → coefficient significantly ≠ 0. Year: t = 10.17 → strong; Qtr1 (no-trend fit): t = 0.03 → useless.
Range holding the true slope with 95% confidence — Year: [1.83, 2.90] per year.
Scientific process of transforming data into insight for better decisions. Why needed: uncertainty + too many alternatives to evaluate.
Fit each k, compare MSE on the same series: k=3 MSE 1737.87 beat k=5's 1935.23 → pick k=3.
Correlation between actual and predicted y; −1..+1. Q5: 0.963 = very strong. R² is its square.
Variation EXPLAINED by the model (Q5: 460.20).
Variation NOT explained — the errors (Q5: 35.62).
Regression df = # predictors · Residual df = n − p − 1 · Total df = n − 1 (1 / 8 / 9 in Q5).
Splits total variation into explained vs unexplained; the F-test compares them.
e = y − ŷ. Positive = actual ABOVE forecast = UNDER-forecast; negative = over-forecast.
Connects points over time — THE chart for time-series data.
Bar = horizontal bars, column = vertical — both compare categorical frequencies.

traps.text: "Use moving averages or exponential smoothing on a trending series" is FALSE — they are appropriate for a HORIZONTAL pattern only; a trend needs regression on t.
"MFE near 0 means the forecasts are accurate" is FALSE — positive and negative errors cancel; gasoline naive has MFE 0.45 with MAE 3.73. MFE reads bias only.
Dividing accuracy measures by n is WRONG when a method can't forecast early periods — divide by n−k (3-yr MA on 5 years: exactly 2 errors, so MSE = Σe²/2).
"Drop period 1 for the trendline MSE too" is FALSE — a fitted regression forecasts EVERY period, so k=0 and Q16's MSE divides by all 5.
"4 quarters need 4 dummy variables" is FALSE — k levels need k−1 dummies; the omitted quarter (Q4) is the baseline captured by the intercept.
"Quarter 4 has a coefficient" is FALSE — Q4's forecast is the intercept alone (Q18: Y4Q4 = 77; umbrella Q4 = 95).
"The naive method is the best simple baseline" is FALSE on the gasoline data — the average of history beat it on MAE, MSE, AND MAPE.
"Exponential smoothing starts at 0" is FALSE — the chain starts ŷ2 = y1 (Q15: first forecast is 234, the first actual).
"Bigger α always reacts better" is FALSE — with heavy random variability a LARGE α chases noise; use small α, and formally pick α by minimum MSE.
"MAPE and MAE always agree" is FALSE — Starbucks has MAE 76 vs the coffee shop's 8, yet a LOWER MPAE (7.0% vs 7.5%): worse absolutely, better relatively.
"Predictive analytics recommends the best action" is FALSE — recommending the best decision under constraints is PRESCRIPTIVE (optimization).
On review Q3 the distractors read "the reader need NOT…" — three options are the LECTURE RULES NEGATED; only 'values with different units or magnitudes' survives.
"A pie chart is best for precise comparisons" is FALSE — bar/column charts compare categorical values; tables give precise values.
"Crosstabulation only works when both variables are qualitative" is FALSE — it works for any mix (qual×qual, qual×quant, quant×quant).
"R² is the correlation coefficient" is FALSE — Multiple R is; R² is its square (Q19: R = .979 → R² = .958, i.e. 95.8% of variation explained).
"Include a dummy for every season" is FALSE — k dummies + intercept is perfect multicollinearity; that is WHY the rule is k−1.
"Seasonal dummies alone handle trending data" is FALSE — same 12 quarters: R² = 0.138 without t, 0.900 with t. Plot first; if it climbs, add the trend term.
"The intercept is the value at time zero, so it's meaningful" is FALSE when t = 0 lies outside the data range — b₀ = 80.46 is a mathematical anchor for the line, not a real year-zero prediction.
"Forecasting MSE and ANOVA's MS Residual are the same number" is FALSE — the exam's forecasting MSE = ΣFE²/n = 35.62/10 = 3.56, while ANOVA MS = 35.62/8 = 4.45 (÷ n−p−1). Read which one is asked.
"A dummy with p = 0.97 still belongs in the model" is FALSE — no-trend fit: Qtr1 p = 0.974 → indistinguishable from zero. High p = no evidence of effect.
"The trend model predicts ANY future year equally well" is FALSE — the notes' fitted line is reliable for years NEAR the data (1–10); far extrapolation degrades.
"Residual df = n − 1" is FALSE — it's n − predictors − 1 (Q5: 10−1−1 = 8); dividing by the wrong df wrecks MS and F.
"A positive forecast error means you over-forecast" is FALSE — e = y − ŷ > 0 means the actual came in ABOVE the forecast (under-forecast).

questions.q: "Constructing a mathematical model to predict future sales from past data" is which analytics type?
Tables should be used when…
questions.a: the values displayed have different units or very different magnitudes ✓ (the other options negate the lecture's rules)

questions.q: Best table for data on TWO variables?
Charts for comparing categorical variables?
questions.a: bar charts AND column charts ✓ (scatter/line are for quantitative/time)

questions.q: Qualitative methods are used when…
questions.a: historical data unavailable or not applicable ✓

questions.a: horizontal ✓ · and MA/ES are appropriate for → horizontal ✓
